Amazon / Zappos 2025

SoleMate: AI Shoe Shopping

Designed an AI-powered footwear shopping app in three weeks from a VP ask to working prototype, combining chat-based AI recommendations with Pinterest-style visual discovery. Drove daily senior director design reviews while iterating in parallel with engineering. Earned VP greenlight, launched in beta on the Zappos app. Patent submitted for contextual auto quick-fill interaction.

Role · UX vision lead
Stack · AWS Bedrock, Claude, Zappos/Amazon/Shopbop catalog
Outcome · Beta launched on Zappos app
IP · Patent submitted

The brief

A VP asked for proof that agentic AI shopping could work for specialty retail, running shoe discovery on the Zappos catalog, in 21 days, from nothing to a working prototype.

Timeline
21 days, zero to VP-level review
Role
Lead UX Designer, designing the vision while engineering built the working prototype in parallel
Cadence
Daily design reviews, with room to pivot the CX mid-stream
Constraint
Built outside the standard storefront ecosystem, a blank canvas, and a tight one

The problem space

AI shopping experiences were dominated by text-heavy chatbots. Runners face complex discovery, gait, arch type, terrain, injuries, style, that traditional filters can't capture. "I have shin splints and I'm training for my first half marathon" doesn't map to any dropdown.

The default

Text-heavy conversational chatbots. Utilitarian, easy to build, and functionally a search bar wearing a personality. No visual richness, no memory, no trust in the answer.

What running shoes actually need

A discovery experience with the visual richness of Pinterest and the judgment of an in-store expert, one that gets smarter about you the more you use it.

Core principles, not a feature list

01

Guided discovery, not a chatbot

Customers won't type paragraphs on mobile, but they'll give more upfront if the experience feels guided and premium rather than like filling out a form.

02

Context that compounds

Saved "boards" carry preferences, returns, and prior picks across sessions. Every visit makes the next one smarter, instead of resetting to zero.

03

Visual-first, always

Full-bleed imagery and interactive product views. A tactile, visual category deserves an experience that doesn't feel utilitarian.

Key design decisions

Pills over free textBasis for patent

Open-ended text entry tested early, but shopping intent is often half-formed. Pills like "Trail running," "Under $150," "Wide fit" give people language they didn't know they needed.

Contextual auto quick-fillPatent submitted

Pills pre-fill from context, not just inferred preference and past purchases, but also where a customer is in their journey and when they engage the chat. Someone who bought stability shoes for overpronation sees "Stability," "Road running," "Similar to [last purchase]" surfaced automatically.

Intent over attributes

Runners think in intent, "I'm training for a marathon," "I have shin splints", not catalog language like shoe drop or stack height. The input layer translates natural language to attributes behind the scenes.

Recommendation transparency

Early builds surfaced a shortlist with no explanation. The CX evolved to reiterate the request, justify the top pick in one sentence, and show which attributes actually matched.

Boards as memory

Instead of a linear chat log, saved boards act as themed collections a customer builds over time, "Marathon training," "Casual daily," "Rocky terrain trail running."

The experience

Five flows from the working prototype, mapped to what each was built to prove.

Discovery & Getting Started

an AI-powered dual experience combining a dynamically refreshing browse feed with an interactive shopping chat, creating a synergistic discovery loop where conversations instantly enhance personalized content and recommendations in real time.

→→→

Product Recommendations & Refinement

AI-driven chat interprets customer input, automatically applying contextual filters to curate and refine product selections, streamlining discovery without manual effort.

→→→

Product Evaluation & Education

AI facilitates confident purchasing through interactive 3D product exploration and on-demand Q&A, eliminating information overload while enhancing evaluation.

→→→

Re-engagement

AI proactively nurtures customer engagement through timely, personalized content updates and smart action prompts that anticipate next purchase steps.

→→→

Image Upload

customers can search visually, uploading a photo to surface similar products instead of describing what they want in words.

→→→

Outfit Visualizer

elevates the shopping experience by providing AI-powered, context-aware outfit inspiration with seamless purchase options for individual items or complete looks.

→→→

The hard part

With engineering building in parallel, there was no "design it all, then hand it off." Every decision had immediate downstream consequences, and daily reviews meant leadership could redirect the vision mid-build without warning.

"Monday's mocks became Tuesday's code." Holding the full system architecture in her head while making surgical adjustments to individual screens, without breaking the coherence of the whole.

Pilot validation

Zappos ran two targeted pilots after leadership approval, an internal employee study and controlled demos at a Brooklyn running pop-up. The findings validated the original design bets and sharpened a few of them.

Pilot learningOriginal responsePost-pilot evolution
Customers want to know "why this shoe" "Why" pills on product cards Added a one-line justification for the top pick, plus request reiteration
Willing to invest time upfront for guided refinement Pill-based guided input Sequential single-select refinement, ask the next most useful question
Shop by intent and pain, not attributes Natural-language input layer Supplemented with expert running guides mapping intent to attributes
Don't want to type on mobile Pill prompts to reduce typing Confirmed, lean further into guided pills, minimize free text
Want social proof and trending signals Visual discovery feed with editorial content Backlogged, trending indicators, influencer signals, purchase velocity

  • →Greenlit by VP leadership to proceed straight into development
  • →Continued building the CX for the pilot after greenlight, working from the same vision through to pilot-ready
  • →Consulted on handoff, bringing pilot findings back to the Zappos design team to shape what they iterated on for the beta that's live today
  • →Adopted as a reference across the broader design org for teams exploring AI shopping integration

What shipped

The Zappos team took the pilot findings and built a simplified, chat-first version for launch, a single Q&A thread rather than the fuller visual, pill-based, board-driven experience from the original vision. The core instincts carried through: guided questions over open text, and a comparison table that echoes the original attribute-transparency work.

→→→

Why this matters beyond running shoes

01

A reference architecture for AI shopping CX

Visual-first, pill-based, context-compounding, this became the starting point other teams reach for when adding AI to a shopping experience.

02

A proof point for speed

Zero to a shipped prototype in 21 days, using agentic AI development tools to compress months of work into weeks.

03

A design philosophy for agentic experiences

The best AI shopping experiences don't look like chatbots, they look like a really good shopping experience that happens to know you.

04

A pattern that generalizes

Intent-based discovery, guided refinement, visual richness, and persistent context apply anywhere expertise matters, skincare, furniture, outdoor gear, baby products. SoleMate isn't a shoe app; it's a proof of concept for AI-powered specialty retail.
